PullRequest.Title: Add word wrap control to Agents editors
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add an independent, experiment-controlled `sessions.editor.wordWrap` setting with `off`, `on`, and `inherit` values
- apply the setting to code, diff, and multi-diff editors in the Agents window
- add a checked **Word Wrap** action to Agents multi-diff editor overflow menus
- keep inherited wrapping synchronized with the effective editor word-wrap state

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`
- 28 focused unit tests
- `git diff --check`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call chain and strict-reference notification are explicit in the repository, and both changed callers demonstrably issue back-to-back writes. Virtualization bounds cardinality to currently bound entries, so exact duration varies with viewport/content, but the doubled per-entry work is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous option validation, object allocation, and updateOptions calls for both embedded code editors in every currently bound multi-diff item
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each setter notification fans out across the effective set of bound/visible multi-diff entries; each entry updates two Monaco code editors. The new setter is called directly after setViewMode, so each activation/visibility callback or preference change causes two O(bound diff entries) passes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous CPU/allocation work and editor-switch or preference-toggle latency, with the cost growing with the number of compact diff entries instantiated in the viewport.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The multi-diff editor received one _diffLayoutOptions write from setViewMode per layout application, producing one options propagation pass across bound entries.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: setDiffWordWrap always writes a second fresh _diffLayoutOptions object. Both SessionsDiffEditorLayoutContribution and SessionChangesEditor call it immediately after setViewMode, so even when neither effective value changed, the same bound entries process another full options update.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added _diffLayoutOptions.set at lines 133-136 introduces a second observable write, while added calls at src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/browser/diffEditor.sessions.contribution.ts:145 and src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/browser/sessionChangesEditor.ts:285 place that write immediately after the existing setViewMode write on hot editor activation/visibility and settings autoruns.
Findings.Title: [medium] Coalesce the multi-diff option writes
Findings.Impact: With a multi-diff/Changes editor showing many compact entries, switching active editors, changing visible editors, or changing either layout preference synchronously traverses every bound diff twice and updates both inner editors twice, adding avoidable UI-thread work and potential interaction jank.
Findings.Evidence: MultiDiffEditorWidget._diffLayoutOptions is an observableValue using strict object equality, so the fresh object at this line always notifies. MultiDiffEditorWidgetImpl derives a fresh options override from it; DiffEditorItemTemplate has one autorun per bound item that calls DiffEditorWidget.updateOptions; DiffEditorEditors then updates both original and modified CodeEditorWidgets. The changed callers at diffEditor.sessions.contribution.ts:144-145 and sessionChangesEditor.ts:284-285 invoke setViewMode and setDiffWordWrap sequentially, yielding two notifications/passes.
Findings.Recommendation: Expose one setter that applies view mode and word wrap in a single _diffLayoutOptions.set (and skip the write when the resulting values are unchanged), then use it from both callers; alternatively add equality guards and batch the two fields in one observable transaction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or restoring the Agents Changes editor with a multi-diff list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor creation installs an autorun that synchronously calls setViewMode and then setDiffWordWrap; once diff item templates are bound, each options notification reaches DiffEditorItemTemplate and both embedded code editors before the UI settles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is the number of currently bound virtualized diff entries, not every changed file; each bound entry owns one diff editor with two code editors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All option propagation is synchronous and serialized on the UI thread. The two writes are sequential rather than batched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Virtualization limits live templates to rendered/kept-alive entries. There is no equality/coalescing at _diffLayoutOptions because each setter creates a new object; inner editors can reject equal computed options only after cloning, validating, and traversing them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the observable write, per-template autorun, DiffEditorWidget update, and two inner CodeEditorWidget updates are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cost depends on viewport size and diff-entry heights, but compact change lists can bind several embedded diff editors and the duplicate traversal is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated synchronous work: the PR adds a second collection-wide options notification instead of applying both fields atomically.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switching active/visible editors while an Agents multi-diff editor remains visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: onDidActiveEditorChange/onDidVisibleEditorsChange synchronously invokes applyLayout, which calls setDiffEditorViewMode and setDiffEditorWordWrap back-to-back on each visible MultiDiffEditor before the editor-change handling completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible editor panes multiplied by currently bound diff entries in each visible multi-diff pane, with two inner code editors per entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread fan-out; event callbacks and the two setter passes are serialized with no batching.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Values are usually warm and unchanged on tab switches, but fresh option object identities defeat the outer observable's equality check; downstream scalar derivations may suppress later layout work only after per-entry option reconstruction and code-editor update attempts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both event subscriptions and sequential setters are explicit, and strict-reference observable equality is confirmed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workbench layouts usually contain few visible panes, while bound compact entries vary; this affects severity but not the doubled mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable as the same finding because the diff doubles an existing O(bound entries) synchronous pass on a common interaction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggling Word Wrap from the Agents multi-diff overflow menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action reads the focused editor state, awaits persistence of sessions.editor.wordWrap, then the configuration event synchronously propagates the new option to visible code, text-diff, and multi-diff editors. The actual wrap relayout is required, but the multi-diff path first performs an unchanged view-mode pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist sessions.editor.wordWrap through IConfigurationService.updateValue and ConfigurationEditing.writeConfiguration to the applicable user settings resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one queued configuration write per menu toggle; no per-file or per-editor filesystem fan-out
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no Sessions Word Wrap action or sessions.editor.wordWrap persistence operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action awaits the write before its promise resolves; the resulting configuration event drives editor relayout. This bounded persistence is intentional for the user setting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One configuration update per click; propagation scales with visible panes and, for each multi-diff pane, its bound virtualized entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration writes use the existing serialized ConfigurationEditing queue. Editor propagation after the event is synchronous; multi-diff view-mode and wrap writes are sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration inspection/model data is warm in memory; the target settings text model may be cached, but each distinct toggle still performs a queued persisted update. Multi-diff option notifications are not coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the filesystem/configuration boundary and propagation path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Settings-file latency varies by local/remote profile, but call cardinality is one and does not scale with changed files.
Scenarios.Verdict: The single persisted write is bounded and not itself a regression. The avoidable extra synchronous multi-diff pass is covered by the reported coalescing finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Applying the experiment value to visible standalone code and text-diff editors in the Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Contribution startup, editor activation/visibility events, or a configuration change loop over visible panes and synchronously call updateOptions on supported controls.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the number of visible editor panes; text-diff panes contain two code editors, while standalone code panes contain one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous sequential loop on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CodeEditor configuration detects unchanged options and stops after cloning/migration; observable configuration reads are in-memory. No collection cache or network cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for reachability and bounded cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible pane count is normally small, and unchanged standalone updates are suppressed before rendering; no realistic high-impact regression was established for this branch alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: applying the option is required behavior, cardinality is small, and unchanged inner code-editor options are guarded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files. Submitted one medium-confidence/high-mechanism-confidence repeated-work finding for the back-to-back multi-diff option notifications. Checked startup, editor switching, preference toggling, visible-editor propagation, virtualization, configuration persistence, cache behavior, and concurrency; no additional actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
